question: Which Fundamental Right was deleted by The Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Property**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 44th Constitutional amendment act 1978 deleted the right to property__ from the list of Fundamental Rights.
 
• Right to Property is no more a fundamental right, only a legal right.
 
• The right to property was listed under Article 31 before its deletion.
 
• At present right to property is listed under Article 300A as a legal right.
 
• In the original constitution, there were seven categories of fundamental rights in India.
 
• After the deletion of the Right to property by the 44th Amendment, it was reduced to six.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Now there are six categories of fundamental rights in India.
 
 
• Right to Equality.
 
• Right to Freedom.
 
• Right against Exploitation.
 
• Right to Freedom of Religion.
 
• Cultural and Educational Rights.
 
• Right to Constitutional Remedies.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Fundamental rights are justiciable.
 
• The Supreme court and the High Courts are considered as the guardians of Fundamental rights in India.
